items.title: 2026. 11. 05. APT29 watering hole támadása ismert iOS és Android sérülékenységeket használt ki A Sekoia vizsgálata egy kiterjedt, mobileszközöket célzó „watering hole” kampányt ír le. A módszer lénye…
items.summary: Sekoia reports an extensive watering-hole campaign attributed to APT29 that targeted mobile devices by exploiting known iOS and Android vulnerabilities.

items.title: 2026-019: Critical Vulnerability in GitLab Community and Enterprise Editions
items.summary: GitLab patched a critical flaw allowing unauthenticated remote code execution on GitLab servers; CERT-EU urges prioritised patching of internet-facing instances and compromise assessment.

items.title: 2026-017: Critical Vulnerability in Cisco Secure Email Gateway
items.summary: A critical flaw in the AMP feature of Cisco Secure Email Gateway allows unauthenticated remote attackers to write files and run commands as root; Cisco PSIRT confirms active exploitation.

items.title: 2026-018: Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP
items.summary: PHP fixed two critical vulnerabilities enabling unauthenticated RCE in versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35; PoCs are circulating, raising exploitation risk.

items.title: Threat actors use agentic AI tooling to find and abuse exposed secrets
items.summary: Microsoft observed threat actors using the agentic offensive framework ARTEX to scan GitHub for OAuth application secrets, then abusing compromised OAuth apps to act inside victim tenants.

items.title: French bank Credit Mutuel Arkea says €100 million missing after cyberattack
items.summary: French bank Credit Mutuel Arkea reports roughly EUR 100 million missing following a cyberattack.

items.title: 87% say their AI controls need to work better
items.summary: Vanson Bourne survey of 3,600 decision-makers: most report AI systems acting without routine review, and 87% say their organisation needs better ways to approve, monitor and control AI use.

items.title: 99% of repository access tokens never expire
items.summary: BlueFlag Security report finds 99% of repository access tokens never expire, leaving developers, bots and AI coding agents with standing access to code long after work ends.

items.title: 3 Charged in Scheme to Use AI to Impersonate CEOs and Attorneys to Steal $129 Million
items.summary: Three people were charged in a scheme using AI to impersonate CEOs and attorneys, defrauding companies' accounting departments of USD 129 million.

items.title: Threat actor targets Indian fintechs on weekends when defenders aren’t watching
items.summary: CERT-IN warns of a significant escalation in AI-powered attacks against Indian fintechs, with a threat actor deliberately striking on weekends when defender coverage is thin.

items.title: FBI, CISA warn of cyberattacks targeting refrigeration systems
items.summary: FBI and CISA warn that attackers are actively targeting industrial refrigeration and cold-chain monitoring systems worldwide, risking spoilage, equipment damage and fire hazards.

items.title: India flags Chinese-linked AI tools in hacking campaign against financial firms
items.summary: India has flagged Chinese-linked AI tooling used in a hacking campaign against financial firms.

items.title: US Government Email Systems Open to Abuse Thanks to Typos
items.summary: Dark Reading reports that erroneous or outdated DNS records in US government domains leave email systems open to abuse by attackers.

items.title: Fake OpenAI, SpaceX events used to steal Microsoft, Google accounts
items.summary: Attackers are using fake OpenAI, SpaceX and Anthropic event invitations delivered via two phishing-as-a-service platforms to steal Microsoft and Google credentials and session tokens.

items.title: Nearly 1.5 million exposed secrets targeted in new revocation program
items.summary: Truffle Security launched a free Secrets Revocation Program helping API key issuers revoke about 1.4 million publicly exposed but still-valid secrets.

items.title: Tageszusammenfassung - 05.11.2026
items.summary: CERT.at daily report covers a second European wave of refrigeration system manipulations (none observed in Austria) and a confirmed DreamHost data breach.

items.title: Kühlanlagenmanipulationen: Zweite Runde
items.summary: CERT.at details a second wave of attacks on refrigeration systems across Europe, initially targeting Danfoss and Copeland/Dixell XWEB devices in France; Austria reports exposure now minimal.

items.title: Email threat landscape: Q3 2026 trends and insights
items.summary: Microsoft's Q3 2026 email threat report notes a sharp rise in phishing, declining QR code phishing, recovering CAPTCHA-gated phishing, and abuse of spoofed business-service sender domains via security overrides.

items.title: Post-Quantum Questions to Ask Your Vendors
items.summary: CISA, ASD's ACSC and NSA published joint guidance and a quick-reference list of questions to assess vendor readiness for post-quantum cryptography migration.

items.title: US Government Partners Urge Hardening Industrial Refrigeration and Cold Chain Monitoring Systems
items.summary: CISA, FBI, HHS, USDA and DoT issued joint guidance on hardening industrial refrigeration and cold-chain monitoring systems after observing global malicious activity against healthcare, chemical, food and transport operators.

items.title: GPT‑6 Cyber: Advancing the frontier of aligned cybersecurity agents
items.summary: OpenAI introduced GPT-6 Cyber, a cybersecurity model for finding exploitable vulnerabilities and developing fixes, trained to remain within authorised scope.

items.title: A view from Brussels: What the Commission's Work Programme says about 2027 initiatives
items.summary: IAPP analysis of the European Commission's Work Programme and what it signals for 2027 digital and privacy initiatives.

items.title: Investment scams with potential victims in at least 50 countries: over 100 servers seized
items.summary: German-led Europol-supported operation seized over 100 servers behind fraudulent trading websites used in investment scams spanning 50+ countries; losses estimated above EUR 4 million, seven suspects identified.

items.title: Security certification is a snapshot, and buyers read too much into it
items.summary: Researchers argue Common Criteria and FIPS-140 certificates are point-in-time snapshots: roughly 6 in 10 vulnerabilities matched to certified products were disclosed after certification.

items.title: Rental phishing sites use live chat to win over hesitant travelers
items.summary: Fortra took down phishing sites cloning rental platforms with copied listings, reviews and live chat support to harvest credentials and card data from travellers.

items.title: AI agents are a ‘bane’ for some website operators, says Cloudflare
items.summary: Cloudflare's CEO says AI agents are a growing burden on website operators, suggests state actors likely exploited the PHP2SHELL issue long ago, and questions the future of containers.

items.title: South Korea stocks hit 9-month low as US midterm results spark AI selloff
items.summary: South Korea stocks hit 9-month low as US midterm results spark AI selloff Reuters

items.title: New wave of bomb hoaxes hits dozens of flights across Europe
items.summary: A new wave of bomb hoaxes disrupted dozens of flights across Europe.

items.title: Feds warn grocers: Don't chill on cyber defenses as freezer hacking spree heats up
items.summary: US federal agencies urge grocers and cold-chain operators to harden defences amid a spree of freezer and refrigeration system hacks; no confirmed US supermarket incidents yet.

items.title: US warns of 'ongoing cyber threat' to industrial refrigeration systems
items.summary: US authorities warn of an ongoing cyber threat to industrial refrigeration systems across multiple critical sectors.

items.title: Binance hack prompted US regulators to check in on bank systems, sources say
items.summary: Following the Binance hack, US regulators reportedly began checking the resilience of bank systems, per Reuters sources.

items.title: New investments to reduce on-premises security risk
items.summary: Microsoft announced an on-premises security initiative combining guidance, migration support and product investments to reduce on-prem risk.

items.title: Notes from the Asia-Pacific region: Singapore charts course for AI risk management in financial services
items.summary: Singapore is setting out an AI risk management approach for the financial services sector, a possible reference point for other regulators.

items.title: Not a game: Europol and partners target terrorist role-playing online
items.summary: Europol's EU IRU coordinated a referral action day with 16 countries against violent extremist role-playing content in online gaming environments.

items.title: Why is Iran exempting India, China, Qatar, Iraq from Hormuz restrictions?
items.summary: Iran exempts ships from India, China, Qatar and Iraq from Strait of Hormuz restrictions, a move analysts see as politically risky.

items.title: Global tech stocks plunge as US midterms add to AI slowdown fears
items.summary: Global tech stocks fell as US midterm results fuelled expectations of tougher scrutiny of data centre construction and the AI sector.

items.title: Iraq’s al-Zaidi talks to Trump as Baghdad seeks to stay out of war on Iran
items.summary: Iraq's top diplomat urges armed groups to stay out of Iranian retaliation as Baghdad seeks to avoid being drawn into the US-Iran conflict.

items.title: EXCLUSIVE: China's top flash memory chipmaker targets more homegrown tools for new factory, sources say
items.summary: China's top flash memory chipmaker aims to use more domestic equipment in a new factory, per Reuters sources.

items.title: US voters’ warning to European politicians
items.summary: Politico discusses whether the Democratic midterm victory will shift US policy on tariffs and Ukraine support in ways that matter for Europe.

items.title: Don’t try to ‘please the dictator,’ Estonian leader urges Europe about Putin
items.summary: Estonian PM Kristen Michal urges Europe to tighten sanctions on Moscow rather than negotiate with Putin.

items.title: Iran’s security chief meets Putin, delivers message from Khamenei
items.summary: Iran's security chief met Putin in Moscow and delivered a letter from Khamenei amid regional security talks.

items.title: Queens Public Library says ransomware attack disrupted Wi-Fi, on-site computers
items.summary: Queens Public Library confirmed a ransomware attack disrupted Wi-Fi and on-site computers across its 66 branches.

items.title: Ads in Chatbots Have Arrived. Here’s What’s Working—and What’s Not
items.summary: Advertising is entering AI chatbots, with most vendors courting advertisers while Anthropic keeps ads out of Claude.

items.title: Social media giants sue California to overturn law shielding kids 15 and under from compulsive use
items.summary: Google, Meta and TikTok sued California over a law banning platform features deemed psychologically exploitative for users 15 and under.

items.title: Bring a tent, I've got the coffee: Lessons from it-sa
items.summary: Cisco Talos reflects on it-sa in Nuremberg and a German initiative to create a formal IT security apprenticeship programme.

items.title: EU targets large firms to unlock budget deal
items.summary: European Council President Costa proposes targeting large firms as a concession to unlock agreement on the EU's next long-term budget.

items.title: Setting a new standard for responsible AI infrastructure
items.summary: OpenAI published a National Community Compact and Compute Campus Policy Blueprint on responsible AI infrastructure development.
